description: We are CadetForge, a collaborative team from Lahore participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are building a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer focused on interactive learning and lunar or Martian outpost management. Our team has skills in software development, frontend development, game logic, backend development, AI, research, and project coordination.
summary:
CadetForge is "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer", a Moon-colony survival game for children aged 7–12. Over seven days, players walk a 3D lunar surface with a joystick, build structures at glowing pads, and make a final decision each day that changes the colony's five resources: oxygen, power, water, food and radiation protection. Run out and it's Game Over; survive all missions and you win.

Between missions, a Learning Center brings in real science: live space-weather events from NASA DONKI (solar flares and coronal mass ejections) and space-biology studies from NASA OSDR. Space-weather conditions feed into the radiation-risk mechanics, so real events shape gameplay.

It addresses the challenge by teaching systems thinking, trade-offs and space science through play rather than lectures. Guest access needs no email or password, which keeps it child-friendly and privacy-conscious. It runs on web and Android from one Flutter codebase.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Players choose an astronaut, enter the Mission Hub, explore the lunar surface, build at objective pads and manage five colony resources over seven themed days (Outpost Setup, Power Management, Radiation Protection, Water & Life Support, Emergency Response, Food Production, Scientific Exploration). Producing one resource can drain another (e.g. water + electricity → oxygen), so every choice has a consequence. The Learning Center has Moon facts, space safety, astronaut life, live NASA DONKI space weather, and NASA OSDR research.

IMPACT

Makes lunar science and resource planning accessible and fun for ages 7–12, building scientific curiosity, systems thinking and decision-making. Real NASA data keeps the learning current.

HOW IT WORKS

- Frontend: Flutter/Dart (web + Android), with custom-rendered 3D-style scenes and a Three.js lunar-walk scene.

- Backend: Python FastAPI – game rules, mission/resource logic, and a proxy/cache layer for NASA DONKI and OSDR.

- Database/Auth: Supabase (PostgreSQL + anonymous Auth), with a backend guest-account fallback and a SQLite local mode for network reliability.

- Data: NASA DONKI API (space weather) and NASA OSDR (space biology).

CREATIVITY & DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

Real-time space weather directly influences in-game radiation risk. Name-only guest sign-in (the name stays on the device), touch and keyboard controls, tilting 3D mission carousel, offline/fallback handling, and age-appropriate language.

TEAM

Monam Majeed (Application Developer, Flutter), Aneeza Mustafa (Frontend), Muhammad Awais (Backend), and Laiba Saleem (Team Lead, Backend Developer, Presentation & Resource Management).
